title: Trumpeter Marvin Peterson: the koto in Japan and his health habits
summary: Gil describes Marvin Peterson's stage manner, his playing a koto in Tokyo and his health regimen.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Well let's see, I was on trumpet. Johnny Coles and (Marvin?) Peterson.
Now Marvin went to Japan with you right?
He can't be with me this next Monday, so I don't know who I'm going to have.
And he has that kind of ballet stance. (LAUGHTER). Playing in his bare feet.

He decides what he wants to put, to put that song, he gets a grasp of/you know. What he wants to do with it and sometimes he'll come out in front and have the horn in his hand and he'll know that there's no sound he can get on that horn that he wants to hear so he'll sing for a few minutes, you know.

And in Japan he played that Koto The Japanese Koto. He played one of those. He never played it before and the man who gave the concerts rented one for him and the first concert we played in Tokyo out he come on the stage and sat down and instead of playing the trumpet started played the Koto.
And it worked alright with you?
Well I got a little disturbed about him at the concert on Henry Street because he kept going, getting up and going off stage.
Yes, he wouldn't play that day too much. I had to ask him to play. I was surprised we had a couple of lulls there and I thought why isn't Marvin playing. So I gave him a little signal.
And I thought, my goodness, is he going back sniffing? Is he going off sniffing?
Oh he's a straight health man. He's a, he doesn't take anything.
I couldn't think of any reason why he would have to get up.
He drinks water. (LAUGHTER). He eats only health cereal. His wife bakes health bread which he, you know, he eats a lot of. You know, he's usually on a health kick.
Well I think he did it at least three times.
